title.narrative: Enhanced sustainability, coverage, benefits adequacy and social welfare services contributing to work-life balance for workers with family responsibilities

description.narrative: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed significant gaps in Georgia’s care sector and social protection system. ILO is supporting efforts to strengthen long-term care provision, improve labour conditions in the care workforce, and introduce unemployment benefits through tripartite social dialogue. The pandemic underscored the vulnerabilities of older people and other groups in need of support services. It also revealed systemic weaknesses, such as fragmented service delivery, uncoordinated policies, and a shortage of qualified care workers, most of whom are women. To address these challenges, the ILO, as part of a joint UN initiative, is supporting a review of labour relations in the care sector to improve working conditions, an assessment of financing and budgeting for community-based care services, promoting deinstitutionalization and more sustainable care models and policy coordination efforts to ensure better integration of care services across sectors. Georgia lacks an unemployment benefit system, leaving workers without income support during job transitions. A 2023 EU country report recommended establishing a comprehensive and sustainable social protection system, including unemployment benefits and minimum income schemes. The ILO, in partnership with Expertise France, is providing technical assistance for the design of an unemployment insurance scheme; facilitating tripartite dialogue to shape policy scenarios and draft new unemployment benefit legislation and supporting the integration of unemployment benefits with active labour market policies to enhance job reintegration. Georgia has yet to ratify the ILO Maternity Protection Convention (No. 183). The ILO supports a trade union-led campaign to advocate for ratification, ensuring improved maternity rights and protections for working women. Through these efforts, the ILO aims to strengthen Georgia’s care sector, expand social protection, and promote gender equality, aligning with international labour standards.
